blocks.html_en: In light of the internalism/externalism distinction, let us revisit the eliminativist challenge raised in §5.1: what explanatory value does intentional description add to formal-syntactic description? Internalists can respond that suitable formal syntactic manipulations determine and maybe even constitute narrow contents, so that internalist intentional description is already implicit in suitable formal syntactic description (cf. Field 2001: 75). Perhaps this response vindicates intentional realism, perhaps not. Crucially, though, no such response is available to content externalists. Externalist intentional description is not implicit in formal syntactic description, because one can hold formal syntax fixed while varying wide content. Thus, content externalists who espouse CTM+FSC must say what we gain by supplementing formal-syntactic explanations with intentional explanations. Once we accept that mental computation is sensitive to syntax but not semantics, it is far from clear that any useful explanatory work remains for wide content. Fodor addresses this challenge at various points, offering his most systematic treatment in The Elm and the Expert (1994). See Arjo (1996), Aydede (1998), Aydede and Robbins (2001), Wakefield (2002); Perry (1998), and Wakefield (2002) for criticism. See Rupert (2008) and Schneider (2005) for positions close to Fodor’s. Dretske (1993) and Shea (2018, pp. 197–226) pursue alternative strategies for vindicating the explanatory relevance of wide content.

blocks.html_en: 5.3 Content-involving computation

sentences.en: 5.3 Content-involving computation
sentences.zh: 5.3 涉及计算的内容

blocks.html_en: The perceived gulf between computational description and intentional description animates many writings on CTM. A few philosophers try to bridge the gulf using computational descriptions that individuate computational states in representational terms. These descriptions are content-involving, to use Christopher Peacocke’s (1994) terminology. On the content-involving approach, there is no rigid demarcation between computational and intentional description. In particular, certain scientifically valuable descriptions of mental activity are both computational and intentional. Call this position content-involving computationalism.

sentences.en: The perceived gulf between computational description and intentional description animates many writings on CTM.
sentences.zh: 计算描述和意向描述之间的明显鸿沟激发了许多有关 CTM 的著作。

sentences.en: A few philosophers try to bridge the gulf using computational descriptions that individuate computational states in representational terms.
sentences.zh: 一些哲学家试图使用计算描述来弥合鸿沟，这些计算描述以表征术语来区分计算状态。

sentences.en: These descriptions are content-involving, to use Christopher Peacocke’s (1994) terminology.
sentences.zh: 用 Christopher Peacocke（1994）的术语来说，这些描述是涉及内容的。

sentences.en: On the content-involving approach, there is no rigid demarcation between computational and intentional description.
sentences.zh: 在涉及内容的方法中，计算描述和有意描述之间没有严格的界限。

sentences.en: In particular, certain scientifically valuable descriptions of mental activity are both computational and intentional.
sentences.zh: 特别是，某些对心理活动具有科学价值的描述既是计算性的，也是有意的。

sentences.en: Call this position content-involving computationalism.
sentences.zh: 将此立场称为内容涉及计算主义。

blocks.html_en: Content-involving computationalists need not say that all computational description is intentional. To illustrate, suppose we describe a simple Turing machine that manipulates symbols individuated by their geometric shapes. Then the resulting computational description is not plausibly content-involving. Accordingly, content-involving computationalists do not usually advance content-involving computation as a general theory of computation. They claim only that some important computational descriptions are content-involving.

sentences.en: Content-involving computationalists need not say that all computational description is intentional.
sentences.zh: 涉及内容的计算学家不必说所有计算描述都是有意的。

sentences.en: To illustrate, suppose we describe a simple Turing machine that manipulates symbols individuated by their geometric shapes.
sentences.zh: 为了说明这一点，假设我们描述一个简单的图灵机，它可以操纵按几何形状划分的符号。

sentences.en: Then the resulting computational description is not plausibly content-involving.
sentences.zh: 那么由此产生的计算描述似乎并不涉及内容。

sentences.en: Accordingly, content-involving computationalists do not usually advance content-involving computation as a general theory of computation.
sentences.zh: 因此，涉及内容的计算学家通常不会将涉及内容的计算作为一种通用的计算理论来推进。

sentences.en: They claim only that some important computational descriptions are content-involving.
sentences.zh: 他们只是声称一些重要的计算描述是内容涉及的。

blocks.html_en: One can develop content-involving computationalism in an internalist or externalist direction. Internalist content-involving computationalists hold that some computational descriptions identify mental states partly through their narrow contents. Murat Aydede (2005) recommends a position along these lines. Externalist content-involving computationalism holds that certain computational descriptions identify mental states partly through their wide contents. Tyler Burge (2010a: 95–101), Christopher Peacocke (1994, 1999), and Mark Sprevak (2010) espouse this position. Oron Shagrir (2001, 2020, 2022) advocates a content-involving computationalism that is neutral between internalism and externalism.

sentences.en: One can develop content-involving computationalism in an internalist or externalist direction.
sentences.zh: 人们可以在内在主义或外在主义方向上发展涉及计算主义的内容。

sentences.en: Internalist content-involving computationalists hold that some computational descriptions identify mental states partly through their narrow contents.
sentences.zh: 涉及内容的内在主义计算主义者认为，一些计算描述部分地通过其狭隘的内容来识别心理状态。

sentences.en: Murat Aydede (2005) recommends a position along these lines.
sentences.zh: Murat Aydede (2005) 建议采取这样的立场。

sentences.en: Externalist content-involving computationalism holds that certain computational descriptions identify mental states partly through their wide contents.
sentences.zh: 涉及计算主义的外在主义内容认为，某些计算描述部分地通过其广泛的内容来识别心理状态。

sentences.en: Tyler Burge (2010a: 95–101), Christopher Peacocke (1994, 1999), and Mark Sprevak (2010) espouse this position.
sentences.zh: Tyler Burge (2010a: 95–101)、Christopher Peacocke (1994, 1999) 和 Mark Sprevak (2010) 支持这一立场。

sentences.en: Oron Shagrir (2001, 2020, 2022) advocates a content-involving computationalism that is neutral between internalism and externalism.
sentences.zh: Oron Shagrir（2001、2020、2022）主张一种在内部主义和外部主义之间保持中立的内容涉及计算主义。

blocks.html_en: Externalist content-involving computationalists typically cite cognitive science practice as a motivating factor. For example, perceptual psychology describes the perceptual system as computing an estimate of some object’s size from retinal stimulations and from an estimate of the object’s depth. Perceptual “estimates” are identified representationally, as representations of specific distal sizes and depths. Quite plausibly, representational relations to specific distal sizes and depths do not supervene on internal neurophysiology. Quite plausibly, then, perceptual psychology type-identifies perceptual computations through wide contents. So externalist content-involving computationalism seems to harmonize well with current cognitive science.

sentences.en: Externalist content-involving computationalists typically cite cognitive science practice as a motivating factor.

blocks.html_en: A major challenge facing content-involving computationalism concerns the interface with standard computationalism formalisms, such as the Turing machine. How exactly do content-involving descriptions relate to the computational models found in logic and computer science? Philosophers usually assume that these models offer non-intentional descriptions. If so, that would be a major and perhaps decisive blow to content-involving computationalism.

sentences.en: A major challenge facing content-involving computationalism concerns the interface with standard computationalism formalisms, such as the Turing machine.
sentences.zh: 涉及计算主义的内容面临的一个主要挑战涉及与标准计算主义形式主义（例如图灵机）的接口。

sentences.en: How exactly do content-involving descriptions relate to the computational models found in logic and computer science?
sentences.zh: 涉及内容的描述与逻辑和计算机科学中的计算模型究竟有何关系？

sentences.en: Philosophers usually assume that these models offer non-intentional descriptions.
sentences.zh: 哲学家通常假设这些模型提供了无意识的描述。

sentences.en: If so, that would be a major and perhaps decisive blow to content-involving computationalism.
sentences.zh: 如果是这样，这将是对涉及计算主义的内容的重大且也许是决定性的打击。

blocks.html_en: Arguably, though, many familiar computational formalisms allow a content-involving rather than formal syntactic construal. To illustrate, consider the Turing machine. One can individuate the “symbols” comprising the Turing machine alphabet non-semantically, through factors akin to geometric shape. But does Turing’s formalism require a non-semantic individuative scheme? Arguably, the formalism allows us to individuate symbols partly through their contents. Of course, the machine table for a Turing machine does not explicitly cite semantic properties of symbols (e.g., denotations or truth-conditions). Nevertheless, the machine table can encode mechanical rules that describe how to manipulate symbols, where those symbols are type-identified in content-involving terms. In this way, the machine table dictates transitions among content-involving states without explicitly mentioning semantic properties. Aydede (2005) suggests an internalist version of this view, with symbols type-identified through their narrow contents.[5] Rescorla (2017a) develops the view in an externalist direction, with symbols type-identified through their wide contents. He argues that some Turing-style models describe computational operations over externalistically individuated Mentalese symbols.[6]

sentences.en: Arguably, though, many familiar computational formalisms allow a content-involving rather than formal syntactic construal.
sentences.zh: 然而，可以说，许多熟悉的计算形式主义允许涉及内容而不是形式的句法解释。

sentences.en: To illustrate, consider the Turing machine.

sentences.en: But does Turing’s formalism require a non-semantic individuative scheme?
sentences.zh: 但是图灵的形式主义需要非语义的个体方案吗？

sentences.en: Arguably, the formalism allows us to individuate symbols partly through their contents.
sentences.zh: 可以说，形式主义允许我们部分地通过符号的内容来个体化符号。

sentences.zh: 当然，图灵机的机器表没有明确引用符号的语义属性（例如，符号或真值条件）。

sentences.zh: 尽管如此，机器表可以对描述如何操作符号的机械规则进行编码，其中这些符号以涉及内容的术语进行类型识别。

sentences.zh: 通过这种方式，机器表规定了涉及内容的状态之间的转换，而无需明确提及语义属性。

sentences.en: Aydede (2005) suggests an internalist version of this view, with symbols type-identified through their narrow contents.[5] Rescorla (2017a) develops the view in an externalist direction, with symbols type-identified through their wide contents.
sentences.zh: Aydede（2005）提出了这种观点的内在主义版本，通过其狭窄的内容来识别符号类型。 [5] Rescorla（2017a）从外在主义的方向发展了这一观点，通过其广泛的内容来识别符号的类型。

blocks.html_en: In principle, one might embrace both externalist content-involving computational description and formal syntactic description. One might say that these two kinds of description occupy distinct levels of explanation. Peacocke suggests such a view. Other content-involving computationalists regard formal syntactic descriptions of the mind more skeptically. For example, Burge questions what explanatory value formal syntactic description contributes to certain areas of scientific psychology (such as perceptual psychology). From this viewpoint, the eliminativist challenge posed in §5.1 has matters backwards. We should not assume that formal syntactic descriptions are explanatorily valuable and then ask what value intentional descriptions contribute. We should instead embrace the externalist intentional descriptions offered by current cognitive science and then ask what value formal syntactic description contributes.

sentences.en: In principle, one might embrace both externalist content-involving computational description and formal syntactic description.
sentences.zh: 原则上，人们可以同时接受涉及计算描述的外在内容和形式句法描述。

sentences.zh: 例如，伯吉质疑正式句法描述对科学心理学的某些领域（例如感知心理学）有什么解释价值。

sentences.zh: 相反，我们应该接受当前认知科学提供的外在意向描述，然后询问形式句法描述有何价值。

blocks.html_en: Proponents of formal syntactic description often respond by citing implementation mechanisms. Externalist description of mental activity presupposes that suitable causal-historical relations between the mind and the external physical environment are in place. But surely we want a “local” description that ignores external causal-historical relations, a description that reveals underlying causal mechanisms. Fodor (1987, 1994) argues in this way to motivate the formal syntactic picture. For possible externalist responses to the argument from implementation mechanisms, see Burge (2010b), Rescorla (2017b), Shea (2013), and Sprevak (2010). For an argument that current cognitive science practice does indeed assign an important explanatory role to formal syntax, see Calzavarini and Paternoster (2022). Debate over the explanatory value of formal syntax, and more generally over the relation between computation and representation, seems likely to continue into the indefinite future.

blocks.html_en: 6. Alternative conceptions of computation

sentences.en: Alternative conceptions of computation

blocks.html_en: The literature offers several alternative conceptions, usually advanced as foundations for CTM. In many cases, these conceptions overlap with one another or with the conceptions considered above.

blocks.html_en: 6.1 Information-processing

sentences.en: 6.1 Information-processing
sentences.zh: 6.1 信息处理

blocks.html_en: It is common for cognitive scientists to describe computation as “information-processing”. It is less common for proponents to clarify what they mean by “information” or “processing”. Lacking clarification, the description is little more than an empty slogan.

sentences.en: It is common for cognitive scientists to describe computation as “information-processing”.
sentences.zh: 认知科学家通常将计算描述为“信息处理”。

sentences.en: It is less common for proponents to clarify what they mean by “information” or “processing”.
sentences.zh: 支持者很少澄清“信息”或“处理”的含义。

sentences.en: Lacking clarification, the description is little more than an empty slogan.
sentences.zh: 由于缺乏澄清，这种描述只不过是一句空洞的口号。

blocks.html_en: Claude Shannon introduced a scientifically important notion of “information” in his 1948 article “A Mathematical Theory of Communication”. The intuitive idea is that information measures reduction in uncertainty, where reduced uncertainty manifests as an altered probability distribution over possible states. Shannon codified this idea within a rigorous mathematical framework, laying the foundation for information theory (Cover and Thomas 2006). Shannon information is fundamental to modern engineering. It finds fruitful application within cognitive science, especially cognitive neuroscience. Does it support a convincing analysis of computation as “information-processing”? Consider an old-fashioned tape machine that records messages received over a wireless radio. Using Shannon’s framework, one can measure how much information is carried by some recorded message. There is a sense in which the tape machine “processes” Shannon information whenever we replay a recorded message. Still, the machine does not seem to implement a non-trivial computational model.[7] Certainly, neither the Turing machine formalism nor the neural network formalism offers much insight into the machine’s operations. Arguably, then, a system can process Shannon information without executing computations in any interesting sense.

sentences.en: Claude Shannon introduced a scientifically important notion of “information” in his 1948 article “A Mathematical Theory of Communication”.
sentences.zh: 克劳德·香农 (Claude Shannon) 在其 1948 年的文章“通信的数学理论”中介绍了“信息”这一具有科学重要性的概念。

sentences.en: Does it support a convincing analysis of computation as “information-processing”?

sentences.en: Consider an old-fashioned tape machine that records messages received over a wireless radio.
sentences.zh: 考虑一台老式磁带机，它记录通过无线电接收的消息。

blocks.html_en: Confronted with such examples, one might try to isolate a more demanding notion of “processing”, so that the tape machine does not “process” Shannon information. Alternatively, one might insist that the tape machine executes non-trivial computations. Piccinini and Scarantino (2010) advance a highly general notion of computation—which they dub generic computation—with that consequence.

sentences.zh: 面对这样的例子，人们可能会尝试分离出一种要求更高的“处理”概念，这样磁带机就不会“处理”香农信息。

sentences.en: Alternatively, one might insist that the tape machine executes non-trivial computations.
sentences.zh: 或者，人们可能会坚持认为磁带机执行重要的计算。

blocks.html_en: A second prominent notion of information derives from Paul Grice’s (1989) influential discussion of natural meaning. Natural meaning involves reliable, counterfactual-supporting correlations. For example, tree rings correlate with the age of the tree, and pox correlate with chickenpox. We colloquially describe tree rings as carrying information about tree age, pox as carrying information about chickenpox, and so on. Such descriptions suggest a conception that ties information to reliable, counterfactual-supporting correlations. Fred Dretske (1981) develops this conception into a systematic theory, as do various subsequent philosophers. Does Dretske-style information subserve a plausible analysis of computation as “information-processing”? Consider an old-fashioned bimetallic strip thermostat. Two metals are joined together into a strip. Differential expansion of the metals causes the strip to bend, thereby activating or deactivating a heating unit. Strip state reliably correlates with current ambient temperature, and the thermostat “processes” this information-bearing state when activating or deactivating the heater. Yet the thermostat does not seem to implement any non-trivial computational model. One would not ordinarily regard the thermostat as computing. Arguably, then, a system can process Dretske-style information without executing computations in any interesting sense. Of course, one might try to handle such examples through maneuvers parallel to those from the previous paragraph.

sentences.en: A second prominent notion of information derives from Paul Grice’s (1989) influential discussion of natural meaning.
sentences.zh: 第二个重要的信息概念源自 Paul Grice (1989) 对自然意义的有影响力的讨论。

sentences.en: Natural meaning involves reliable, counterfactual-supporting correlations.

sentences.zh: 我们通俗地将树木年轮描述为携带有关树龄的信息，将痘描述为携带有关水痘的信息，等等。

sentences.en: Consider an old-fashioned bimetallic strip thermostat.
sentences.zh: 考虑一个老式双金属片恒温器。

sentences.zh: 带材状态与当前环境温度可靠相关，并且恒温器在激活或停用加热器时“处理”此信息承载状态。

sentences.en: Arguably, then, a system can process Dretske-style information without executing computations in any interesting sense.

sentences.en: Of course, one might try to handle such examples through maneuvers parallel to those from the previous paragraph.
sentences.zh: 当然，人们可能会尝试通过与上一段类似的策略来处理此类示例。

blocks.html_en: A third prominent notion of information is semantic information, i.e., representational content.[8] Some philosophers hold that a physical system computes only if the system’s states have representational properties (Dietrich 1989; Fodor 1998: 10; Ladyman 2009; Shagrir 2006; Sprevak 2010). In that sense, information-processing is necessary for computation. As Fodor memorably puts it, “no computation without representation” (1975: 34). However, this position is debatable. Chalmers (2011) and Piccinini (2008a) contend that a Turing machine might execute computations even though symbols manipulated by the machine have no semantic interpretation. The machine’s computations are purely syntactic in nature, lacking anything like semantic properties. On this view, representational content is not necessary for a physical system to count as computational.

sentences.en: A third prominent notion of information is semantic information, i.e., representational content.[8] Some philosophers hold that a physical system computes only if the system’s states have representational properties (Dietrich 1989; Fodor 1998: 10; Ladyman 2009; Shagrir 2006; Sprevak 2010).
sentences.zh: 信息的第三个重要概念是语义信息，即表征内容。 [8]一些哲学家认为，只有当系统的状态具有表征属性时，物理系统才会进行计算（Dietrich 1989；Fodor 1998：10；Ladyman 2009；Shagrir 2006；Sprevak 2010）。

sentences.en: In that sense, information-processing is necessary for computation.
sentences.zh: 从这个意义上说，信息处理对于计算来说是必要的。

sentences.zh: 根据这种观点，表征性内容对于物理系统来说并不是计算性的所必需的。

blocks.html_en: It remains unclear whether the slogan “computation is information-processing” provides much insight. Nevertheless, the slogan seems unlikely to disappear from the literature anytime soon. For further discussion of possible connections between computation and information, see Gallistel and King (2009: 1–26), Lizier, Flecker, and Williams (2013), Miłkowski (2013), Piccinini and Scarantino (2010), and Sprevak (2020).

sentences.en: It remains unclear whether the slogan “computation is information-processing” provides much insight.
sentences.zh: 目前尚不清楚“计算就是信息处理”这句口号是否提供了很多见解。

blocks.html_en: Marr’s three levels have attracted intense philosophical scrutiny. For our purposes, the key point is that Marr’s “computational level” describes a mapping from inputs to outputs, without describing intermediate steps. Marr illustrates his approach by providing “computational level” theories of various perceptual processes, such as edge detection.

sentences.en: Marr’s three levels have attracted intense philosophical scrutiny.
sentences.zh: 马尔的三个层次引起了严格的哲学审视。

sentences.en: For our purposes, the key point is that Marr’s “computational level” describes a mapping from inputs to outputs, without describing intermediate steps.
sentences.zh: 就我们的目的而言，关键点是马尔的“计算级别”描述了从输入到输出的映射，但没有描述中间步骤。

sentences.en: Marr illustrates his approach by providing “computational level” theories of various perceptual processes, such as edge detection.
sentences.zh: 马尔通过提供各种感知过程（例如边缘检测）的“计算级”理论来说明他的方法。

blocks.html_en: Marr’s discussion suggests a functional conception of computation, on which computation is a matter of transforming inputs into appropriate outputs. Frances Egan elaborates the functional conception over a series of articles (1991, 1992, 1999, 2003, 2010, 2014, 2019, 2020). Like Marr, she treats computational description as description of input-output relations. She also claims that computational models characterize a purely mathematical function: that is, a mapping from mathematical inputs to mathematical outputs. She illustrates by considering a visual mechanism (called “Visua”) that computes an object’s depth from retinal disparity. She imagines a neurophysiological duplicate (“Twin Visua”) embedded so differently in the physical environment that it does not represent depth. Visua and Twin Visua instantiate perceptual states with different representational properties. Nevertheless, Egan says, vision science treats Visua and Twin Visua as computational duplicates. Visua and Twin Visua compute the same mathematical function, even though the computations have different representational import in the two cases. Egan concludes that computational modeling of the mind yields an “abstract mathematical description” consistent with many alternative possible representational descriptions. Intentional attribution is just a heuristic gloss upon underlying computational description.

sentences.en: Marr’s discussion suggests a functional conception of computation, on which computation is a matter of transforming inputs into appropriate outputs.
sentences.zh: 马尔的讨论提出了一种计算的功能概念，其中计算是将输入转换为适当的输出的问题。

sentences.en: Frances Egan elaborates the functional conception over a series of articles (1991, 1992, 1999, 2003, 2010, 2014, 2019, 2020).
Like Marr, she treats computational description as description of input-output relations.
sentences.zh: 和马尔一样，她将计算描述视为输入输出关系的描述。

sentences.en: She also claims that computational models characterize a purely mathematical function: that is, a mapping from mathematical inputs to mathematical outputs.
sentences.zh: 她还声称计算模型表征了纯粹的数学函数：即从数学输入到数学输出的映射。

sentences.en: She illustrates by considering a visual mechanism (called “Visua”) that computes an object’s depth from retinal disparity.
sentences.zh: 她通过考虑一种视觉机制（称为“Visua”）来说明，该机制根据视网膜视差计算物体的深度。

sentences.en: She imagines a neurophysiological duplicate (“Twin Visua”) embedded so differently in the physical environment that it does not represent depth.
sentences.zh: 她想象了一个神经生理学复制品（“Twin Visua”）在物理环境中的嵌入方式如此不同，以至于它并不代表深度。

sentences.en: Visua and Twin Visua instantiate perceptual states with different representational properties.
sentences.zh: Visua 和 Twin Visua 用不同的表征属性实例化感知状态。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, Egan says, vision science treats Visua and Twin Visua as computational duplicates.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，伊根表示，视觉科学将 Visua 和 Twin Visua 视为计算副本。

sentences.en: Visua and Twin Visua compute the same mathematical function, even though the computations have different representational import in the two cases.
sentences.zh: Visua 和 Twin Visua 计算相同的数学函数，尽管这两种情况下的计算具有不同的表征意义。

sentences.en: Egan concludes that computational modeling of the mind yields an “abstract mathematical description” consistent with many alternative possible representational descriptions.
sentences.zh: 伊根得出的结论是，心灵的计算模型产生了与许多替代的可能的表征描述相一致的“抽象数学描述”。

sentences.en: Intentional attribution is just a heuristic gloss upon underlying computational description.
sentences.zh: 故意归因只是对底层计算描述的启发式注释。

blocks.html_en: Chalmers (2012) argues that the functional conception neglects important features of computation. As he notes, computational models usually describe more than just input-output relations. They describe intermediate steps through which inputs are transformed into outputs. These intermediate steps, which Marr consigns to the “algorithmic” level, figure prominently in computational models offered by logicians and computer scientists. Restricting the term “computation” to input-output description does not capture standard computational practice.

sentences.en: Chalmers (2012) argues that the functional conception neglects important features of computation.
sentences.zh: Chalmers (2012) 认为泛函概念忽略了计算的重要特征。

sentences.en: As he notes, computational models usually describe more than just input-output relations.
sentences.zh: 正如他指出的，计算模型通常不仅仅描述输入-输出关系。

sentences.en: They describe intermediate steps through which inputs are transformed into outputs.
sentences.zh: 它们描述了将输入转换为输出的中间步骤。

sentences.en: These intermediate steps, which Marr consigns to the “algorithmic” level, figure prominently in computational models offered by logicians and computer scientists.
sentences.zh: 马尔将这些中间步骤归为“算法”级别，在逻辑学家和计算机科学家提供的计算模型中占有重要地位。

sentences.en: Restricting the term “computation” to input-output description does not capture standard computational practice.
sentences.zh: 将术语“计算”限制为输入输出描述并不能捕获标准的计算实践。

blocks.html_en: An additional worry faces functional theories, such as Egan’s, that exclusively emphasize mathematical inputs and outputs. Critics complain that Egan mistakenly elevates mathematical functions, at the expense of intentional explanations routinely offered by cognitive science (Burge 2005; Rescorla 2015; Silverberg 2006; Sprevak 2010). To illustrate, suppose perceptual psychology describes the perceptual system as estimating that some object’s depth is 5 meters. The perceptual depth-estimate has a representational content: it is accurate only if the object’s depth is 5 meters. We cite the number 5 to identify the depth-estimate. But our choice of this number depends upon our arbitrary choice of measurement units. Critics contend that the content of the depth-estimate, not the arbitrarily chosen number through which we theorists specify that content, is what matters for psychological explanation. Egan’s theory places the number rather than the content at explanatory center stage. According to Egan, computational explanation should describe the visual system as computing a particular mathematical function that carries particular mathematical inputs into particular mathematical outputs. Those particular mathematical inputs and outputs depend upon our arbitrary choice of measurement units, so they arguably lack the explanatory significance that Egan assigns to them.

sentences.en: An additional worry faces functional theories, such as Egan’s, that exclusively emphasize mathematical inputs and outputs.
sentences.zh: 函数理论（例如伊根的理论）还面临着另一个担忧，该理论专门强调数学输入和输出。

blocks.html_en: We should distinguish the functional approach, as pursued by Marr and Egan, from the functional programming paradigm in computer science. The functional programming paradigm models evaluation of a complex function as successive evaluation of simpler functions. To take a simple example, one might evaluate \(f(x,y) = (x^{2}+y)\) by first evaluating the squaring function and then evaluating the addition function. Functional programming differs from the “computational level” descriptions emphasized by Marr, because it specifies intermediate computational stages. The functional programming paradigm stretches back to Alonzo Church’s (1936) lambda calculus, continuing with programming languages such as PCF and LISP. It plays an important role in AI and theoretical computer science. Some authors suggest that it offers special insight into mental computation (Klein 2012; Piantadosi, Tenenbaum, and Goodman 2012). However, many computational formalisms do not conform to the functional paradigm: Turing machines; imperative programming languages, such as C; logic programming languages, such as Prolog; and so on. Even though the functional paradigm describes numerous important computations (possibly including mental computations), it does not plausibly capture computation in general.

sentences.en: We should distinguish the functional approach, as pursued by Marr and Egan, from the functional programming paradigm in computer science.
sentences.zh: 我们应该将 Marr 和 Egan 所追求的函数式方法与计算机科学中的函数式编程范式区分开来。

sentences.en: The functional programming paradigm models evaluation of a complex function as successive evaluation of simpler functions.

sentences.en: However, many computational formalisms do not conform to the functional paradigm: Turing machines; imperative programming languages, such as C; logic programming languages, such as Prolog; and so on.

blocks.html_en: 6.3 Structuralism

sentences.en: 6.3 Structuralism
sentences.zh: 6.3 结构主义

blocks.html_en: Many philosophical discussions embody a structuralist conception of computation: a computational model describes an abstract causal structure, without taking into account particular physical states that instantiate the structure. This conception traces back at least to Putnam’s original treatment (1967). Chalmers (1995, 1996a, 2011, 2012) develops it in detail. He introduces the combinatorial-state automaton (CSA) formalism, which subsumes most familiar models of computation (including Turing machines and neural networks). A CSA provides an abstract description of a physical system’s causal topology: the pattern of causal interaction among the system’s parts, independent of the nature of those parts or the causal mechanisms through which they interact. Computational description specifies a causal topology.

sentences.en: Many philosophical discussions embody a structuralist conception of computation: a computational model describes an abstract causal structure, without taking into account particular physical states that instantiate the structure.
sentences.zh: 许多哲学讨论都体现了结构主义的计算概念：计算模型描述了抽象的因果结构，而不考虑实例化该结构的特定物理状态。

sentences.en: This conception traces back at least to Putnam’s original treatment (1967).
sentences.zh: 这个概念至少可以追溯到普特南最初的治疗方法（1967）。

sentences.en: Chalmers (1995, 1996a, 2011, 2012) develops it in detail.
sentences.zh: Chalmers (1995, 1996a, 2011, 2012) 对其进行了详细的发展。

sentences.en: He introduces the combinatorial-state automaton (CSA) formalism, which subsumes most familiar models of computation (including Turing machines and neural networks).
sentences.zh: 他介绍了组合状态自动机 (CSA) 形式，其中包含最熟悉的计算模型（包括图灵机和神经网络）。

sentences.en: A CSA provides an abstract description of a physical system’s causal topology: the pattern of causal interaction among the system’s parts, independent of the nature of those parts or the causal mechanisms through which they interact.
sentences.zh: CSA 提供了物理系统因果拓扑的抽象描述：系统各部分之间因果交互的模式，独立于这些部分的性质或它们交互的因果机制。

sentences.en: Computational description specifies a causal topology.
sentences.zh: 计算描述指定因果拓扑。

blocks.html_en: Chalmers deploys structuralism to delineate a very general version of CTM. He assumes the functionalist view that psychological states are individuated by their roles in a pattern of causal organization. Psychological description specifies causal roles, abstracted away from physical states that realize those roles. So psychological properties are organizationally invariant, in that they supervene upon causal topology. Since computational description characterizes a causal topology, satisfying a suitable computational description suffices for instantiating appropriate mental properties. It also follows that psychological description is a species of computational description, so that computational description should play a central role within psychological explanation. Thus, structuralist computation provides a solid foundation for cognitive science. Mentality is grounded in causal patterns, which are precisely what computational models articulate.

sentences.en: Chalmers deploys structuralism to delineate a very general version of CTM.
sentences.zh: 查尔默斯运用结构主义来描绘 CTM 的一个非常通用的版本。

sentences.en: He assumes the functionalist view that psychological states are individuated by their roles in a pattern of causal organization.
sentences.zh: 他假设功能主义观点认为心理状态是根据其在因果组织模式中的角色而个体化的。

sentences.en: Psychological description specifies causal roles, abstracted away from physical states that realize those roles.
sentences.zh: 心理描述指定了因果角色，从实现这些角色的物理状态中抽象出来。

sentences.en: So psychological properties are organizationally invariant, in that they supervene upon causal topology.
sentences.zh: 因此，心理属性在组织上是不变的，因为它们取决于因果拓扑。

sentences.en: Since computational description characterizes a causal topology, satisfying a suitable computational description suffices for instantiating appropriate mental properties.
sentences.zh: 由于计算描述表征了因果拓扑，因此满足适当的计算描述足以实例化适当的心理属性。

sentences.en: It also follows that psychological description is a species of computational description, so that computational description should play a central role within psychological explanation.
sentences.zh: 还可以得出结论，心理描述是计算描述的一种，因此计算描述应该在心理学解释中发挥核心作用。

sentences.en: Thus, structuralist computation provides a solid foundation for cognitive science.
sentences.zh: 因此，结构主义计算为认知科学提供了坚实的基础。

sentences.en: Mentality is grounded in causal patterns, which are precisely what computational models articulate.
sentences.zh: 心态是以因果模式为基础的，而这正是计算模型所表达的。

blocks.html_en: Structuralism comes packaged with an attractive account of the implementation relation between abstract computational models and physical systems. Under what conditions does a physical system implement a computational model? Structuralists say that a physical system implements a model just in case the model’s causal structure is “isomorphic” to the model’s formal structure. A computational model describes a physical system by articulating a formal structure that mirrors some relevant causal topology. Chalmers elaborates this intuitive idea, providing detailed necessary and sufficient conditions for physical realization of CSAs. Few if any alternative conceptions of computation can provide so substantive an account of the implementation relation.

sentences.en: Structuralism comes packaged with an attractive account of the implementation relation between abstract computational models and physical systems.
sentences.zh: 结构主义对抽象计算模型和物理系统之间的实现关系进行了有吸引力的描述。

sentences.en: Under what conditions does a physical system implement a computational model?

sentences.zh: 结构主义者说，物理系统实现模型只是为了防止模型的因果结构与模型的形式结构“同构”。

sentences.en: A computational model describes a physical system by articulating a formal structure that mirrors some relevant causal topology.
sentences.zh: 计算模型通过阐明反映某些相关因果拓扑的形式结构来描述物理系统。

sentences.en: Chalmers elaborates this intuitive idea, providing detailed necessary and sufficient conditions for physical realization of CSAs.
sentences.zh: 查尔默斯阐述了这一直观的想法，为 CSA 的物理实现提供了详细的充要条件。

sentences.en: Few if any alternative conceptions of computation can provide so substantive an account of the implementation relation.
sentences.zh: 很少有替代的计算概念能够提供如此实质性的实现关系说明。

sentences.zh: 我们可以将结构主义计算主义与上面讨论的其他一些理论进行比较：

blocks.html_en: Machine functionalism. Structuralist computationalism embraces the core idea behind machine functionalism: mental states are functional states describable through a suitable computational formalism. Putnam advances CTM as an empirical hypothesis, and he defends functionalism on that basis. In contrast, Chalmers follows David Lewis (1972) by grounding functionalism in the conceptual analysis of mentalistic discourse. Whereas Putnam defends functionalism by defending computationalism, Chalmers defends computationalism by assuming functionalism.

sentences.en: Machine functionalism.
sentences.zh: 机器功能主义。

sentences.en: Structuralist computationalism embraces the core idea behind machine functionalism: mental states are functional states describable through a suitable computational formalism.
sentences.zh: 结构主义计算主义拥抱机器功能主义背后的核心思想：心理状态是可以通过适当的计算形式主义描述的功能状态。

sentences.en: Putnam advances CTM as an empirical hypothesis, and he defends functionalism on that basis.
sentences.zh: 普特南提出 CTM 作为一种经验假设，并在此基础上捍卫功能主义。

sentences.zh: 相比之下，查尔默斯追随大卫·刘易斯（David Lewis，1972），将功能主义植根于心灵论话语的概念分析中。

blocks.html_en: Although structuralist computationalism is distinct from CTM+FSC, it raises some similar issues. blocks.html_en: 6.4 Mechanistic theories

sentences.en: 6.4 Mechanistic theories
sentences.zh: 6.4 机理理论

blocks.html_en: The mechanistic nature of computation is a recurring theme in logic, philosophy, and cognitive science. Several authors develop this theme into a mechanistic conception of computing systems (Coelho Mollo, 2017; Dewhurst 2016; Fresco 2014, 2017; Miłkowski 2013; Piccinini 2007, 2012, 2015). On Gualtiero Piccinini’s (2015) influential development, a functional mechanism is a system of interconnected components, where each component performs some function within the overall system. Mechanistic explanation proceeds by decomposing the system into parts, describing how the parts are organized into the larger system, and isolating the function performed by each part. A computing system is a functional mechanism of a particular kind: it is a mechanism whose components are functionally organized to process vehicles in accord with rules. Echoing Putnam’s discussion of multiple realizability, Piccinini demands that the rules be medium-independent, in that they abstract away from the specific physical implementations of the vehicles. Computational explanation decomposes the system into parts and describes how each part helps the system process the relevant vehicles. If the system processes discretely structured vehicles, then the computation is digital. If the system processes continuous vehicles, then the computation is analog. Marcin Miłkowski’s (2013) version of the mechanistic approach is similar. He differs from Piccinini by pursuing an “information-processing” gloss, so that computational mechanisms operate over information-bearing states. Miłkowski and Piccinini deploy their respective mechanistic theories to defend computationalism. Piccinini (2020) focuses especially upon neural computation, drawing extensive connections with cognitive neuroscience.

blocks.html_en: 6.5 Pluralism

sentences.en: 6.5 Pluralism
sentences.zh: 6.5 多元主义

blocks.html_en: We have surveyed various contrasting and sometimes overlapping conceptions of computation: classical computation, connectionist computation, neural computation, formal-syntactic computation, content-involving computation, information-processing computation, functional computation, structuralist computation, and mechanistic computation. Each conception yields a different form of computationalism. Each conception has its own strengths and weaknesses. One might adopt a pluralistic stance that recognizes distinct legitimate conceptions. Rather than elevate one conception above the others, pluralists happily employ whichever conception seems useful in a given explanatory context. Edelman (2008) takes a pluralistic line, as does Chalmers (2012) in his most recent discussion.

blocks.html_en: The pluralistic line raises some natural questions. Can we provide a general analysis that encompasses all or most types of computation? Deeper understanding of computation requires us to grapple with these questions.

blocks.html_en: 7.1 Triviality arguments

sentences.en: 7.1 Triviality arguments
sentences.zh: 7.1 琐碎论证

blocks.html_en: A recurring worry is that CTM is trivial, because we can describe almost any physical system as executing computations. Searle (1990) claims that a wall implements any computer program, since we can discern some pattern of molecular movements in the wall that is isomorphic to the formal structure of the program. Putnam (1988: 121–125) defends a less extreme but still very strong triviality thesis along the same lines. Triviality arguments play a large role in the philosophical literature. Anti-computationalists deploy triviality arguments against computationalism, while computationalists seek to avoid triviality.

sentences.en: A recurring worry is that CTM is trivial, because we can describe almost any physical system as executing computations.
sentences.zh: 一个反复出现的担忧是 CTM 是微不足道的，因为我们几乎可以将任何物理系统描述为执行计算。

sentences.en: Searle (1990) claims that a wall implements any computer program, since we can discern some pattern of molecular movements in the wall that is isomorphic to the formal structure of the program.
sentences.zh: Searle (1990) 声称墙可以实现任何计算机程序，因为我们可以辨别墙中分子运动的某些模式，该模式与程序的形式结构同构。

sentences.en: Putnam (1988: 121–125) defends a less extreme but still very strong triviality thesis along the same lines.
sentences.zh: 普特南（Putnam，1988：121-125）沿着同样的思路捍卫了一个不那么极端但仍然非常有力的琐碎论点。

sentences.en: Triviality arguments play a large role in the philosophical literature.
sentences.zh: 琐碎论证在哲学文献中发挥着重要作用。

sentences.en: Anti-computationalists deploy triviality arguments against computationalism, while computationalists seek to avoid triviality.
sentences.zh: 反计算主义者利用琐碎论据来反对计算主义，而计算主义者则力图避免琐碎。

blocks.html_en: Computationalists usually rebut triviality arguments by insisting that the arguments overlook constraints upon computational implementation, constraints that bar trivializing implementations. The constraints may be counterfactual, causal, semantic, or otherwise, depending on one’s favored theory of computation. For example, David Chalmers (1995, 1996a) and B. Jack Copeland (1996) hold that Putnam’s triviality argument ignores counterfactual conditionals that a physical system must satisfy in order to implement a computational model. Other philosophers say that a physical system must have representational properties to implement a computational model (Fodor 1998: 11–12; Ladyman 2009; Sprevak 2010) or at least to implement a content-involving computational model (Rescorla 2013). The details here vary considerably, and computationalists debate amongst themselves exactly which types of computation can avoid which triviality arguments. But most computationalists agree that we can avoid any devastating triviality worries through a sufficiently robust theory of the implementation relation between computational models and physical systems.

blocks.html_en: Pancomputationalism holds that every physical system implements a computational model. This thesis is plausible, since any physical system arguably implements a sufficiently trivial computational model (e.g., a one-state finite state automaton). As Chalmers (2011) notes, pancomputationalism does not seem worrisome for computationalism. What would be worrisome is the much stronger triviality thesis that almost every physical system implements almost every computational model.

blocks.html_en: 7.2 Gödel’s incompleteness theorem

sentences.en: 7.2 Gödel’s incompleteness theorem
sentences.zh: 7.2 哥德尔不完备定理

blocks.html_en: According to some authors, Gödel’s incompleteness theorems show that human mathematical capacities outstrip the capacities of any Turing machine (Nagel and Newman 1958). J.R. Lucas (1961) develops this position into a famous critique of CCTM. Roger Penrose pursues the critique in The Emperor’s New Mind (1989) and subsequent writings. Various philosophers and logicians have answered the critique, arguing that existing formulations suffer from fallacies, question-begging assumptions, and even outright mathematical errors (Bowie 1982; Chalmers 1996b; Feferman 1996; Lewis 1969, 1979; Putnam 1975: 365–366, 1994; Shapiro 2003). There is a wide consensus that this criticism of CCTM lacks any force. It may turn out that certain human mental capacities outstrip Turing-computability, but Gödel’s incompleteness theorems provide no reason to anticipate that outcome.

sentences.en: According to some authors, Gödel’s incompleteness theorems show that human mathematical capacities outstrip the capacities of any Turing machine (Nagel and Newman 1958).
sentences.zh: 一些作者认为，哥德尔不完备定理表明人类的数学能力超过了任何图灵机的能力（Nagel 和 Newman 1958）。

sentences.en: J.R.
Lucas (1961) develops this position into a famous critique of CCTM.
sentences.zh: Lucas (1961) 将这一立场发展成为对 CCTM 的著名批评。

sentences.en: Roger Penrose pursues the critique in The Emperor’s New Mind (1989) and subsequent writings.
sentences.zh: 罗杰·彭罗斯在《皇帝的新思想》（1989）和随后的著作中继续进行批评。

sentences.en: Various philosophers and logicians have answered the critique, arguing that existing formulations suffer from fallacies, question-begging assumptions, and even outright mathematical errors (Bowie 1982; Chalmers 1996b; Feferman 1996; Lewis 1969, 1979; Putnam 1975: 365–366, 1994; Shapiro 2003).
sentences.zh: 许多哲学家和逻辑学家都回应了这一批评，认为现有的表述存在谬误、回避问题的假设，甚至是彻底的数学错误(Bowie 1982; Chalmers 1996b; Feferman 1996; Lewis 1969, 1979; Putnam 1975: 365–366, 1994; Shapiro 2003)。

sentences.zh: 人们普遍认为，这种对CCTM的批评缺乏任何力量。

blocks.html_en: 7.3 Limits of computational modeling

sentences.en: 7.3 Limits of computational modeling
sentences.zh: 7.3 计算模型的局限性

blocks.html_en: Could a computer compose the Eroica symphony? Or discover general relativity? Or even replicate a child’s effortless ability to perceive the environment, tie her shoelaces, and discern the emotions of others? Intuitive, creative, or skillful human activity may seem to resist formalization by a computer program (Dreyfus 1972, 1992). More generally, one might worry that crucial aspects of human cognition elude computational modeling, especially classical computational modeling.

sentences.en: Could a computer compose the Eroica symphony?
sentences.zh: 计算机能谱写英雄交响曲吗？

sentences.en: Or discover general relativity?
sentences.zh: 或者发现广义相对论？

sentences.en: Or even replicate a child’s effortless ability to perceive the environment, tie her shoelaces, and discern the emotions of others?
sentences.zh: 或者甚至复制一个孩子毫不费力地感知环境、系鞋带和辨别他人情绪的能力？

sentences.en: Intuitive, creative, or skillful human activity may seem to resist formalization by a computer program (Dreyfus 1972, 1992).
sentences.zh: 直觉的、创造性的或熟练的人类活动似乎抵制计算机程序的形式化（Dreyfus 1972，1992）。

sentences.en: More generally, one might worry that crucial aspects of human cognition elude computational modeling, especially classical computational modeling.
sentences.zh: 更一般地说，人们可能会担心人类认知的关键方面无法进行计算建模，尤其是经典计算建模。
